         3                  SENATOR KLEIN:    Mr. President,

         7       Senator Sampson.

         8                  SENATOR SAMPSON:    Thank you very

         9       much, Mr. President.

        10                  Earlier today, my colleagues, we

        11       received two bills from the Governor.  One

        12       bill was about 440 pages.  The Governor has

        13       met his constitutional obligation and

        14       responsibility by handing down the deficit

        15       reduction proposal.  The Legislature can now

        16       openly consider it.

        17                  While we have concerns, and we too

        18       have real concerns with these proposals, we

        19       are committed in a bipartisan fashion to close

        20       the budget gap.  And make no bones about it,

        21       we understand what our responsibilities are

        22       and we're going to comply with our

        23       responsibilities.  New York needs us to act

        24       immediately and act now, which we will do.

         1                  It's important for everyone to

         2       understand that this isn't about a Democratic

         3       job or a Republican job or Democratic cuts or

         4       Republican cuts.  It's instead about

         5       bipartisanships, understanding the importance

         6       of us working collectively together to cut

         7       what needs to be cut.

         8                  I believe that we can get this done

         9       and we will get this done.  We will reach a

        10       fiscally balanced budget.  And we understand

        11       the concerns, and we understand the issue with

        12       respect to our bond ratings.

        13                  But at the same time, when we're

        14       talking about midyear school cuts, we're

        15       talking about cuts to these institutions which

        16       have a tremendous impact economically in our

        17       communities, but most of all having school

        18       districts making decisions during this period

        19       of time as to whether or not they can survive

        20       and pass those cuts along to our

        21       constituencies with respect to property taxes.

        22                  Right now we're going to review

        23       what the Governor has sent to us.  We're going

        24       to continue to work together.  And I want to

         9       people walking around the Capitol

        10       congratulating us, when they have children who

        11       are autistic who these cuts will severely

        12       damage some of the services that they have,

        13       they ask us do we have a heart.

        15       thank you very much for your commitment.

        16       We're going to get this done.  We understand

        17       our fiscal responsibilities.  And we're not

        18       going to walk away without dealing with what

        19       the Governor has sent to us.  But once again,

        21       look at this and make sure we can come to a

        22       resolution that is fiscally responsible, not

        23       only for the Governor but for everybody in the

        24       State of New York.

        13       spending in terms of what the people of the

        14       State of New York are demanding from us.

        16       extended every courtesy to us as the

        17       Republican conference as we work our way

        18       through this process.  So, John, I thank you,

        19       I thank you for that.

        21       bottom line is we all understand that we have

        22       to reach a deficit reduction plan within the

        23       next several days.  It's incumbent upon us,

        24       and that's our challenge.

         1                  Just over three weeks ago, Governor

         2       Paterson had us come into the Assembly chamber

         3       to let us know how serious the deficit is.

         4       Quite honestly, it was a nice day, but we all

         5       know how serious the deficit is in New York

         6       State.

         7                  That day, I suggested that the

         8       Governor send us a deficit reduction bill --

         9       not a press release, not a sketchy plan, but

        10       an actual bill.  And he did not do that,

        11       despite the fact that we are asked to come

        12       back in in special session.

        13                  Today he is finally, after

        14       approximately three weeks, sending us a bill.

        15                  While we've waited to take action

        16       on a bill, our conference, our Republican

        17       conference, proposed a plan that works off a

        18       number of the Governor's proposals to address

        19       the $3.2 billion deficit.

        20                  In fact, our conference did come up

        21       with a plan that did exactly that, and the

        22       Governor at times indicated that we were the

        23       conference that was suggesting spending cuts.

        24                  And right now the discussions that

         9       challenge in the next couple of days to work

        10       together in a nonpolitical way.

        24       glad that the Governor finally sent us a
